label: rem:confinement-level-properties
title: $q$-dependence, magic gaps, and the KLR grading of the confinement filtration
html:
q-dependence. The filtration is intrinsically q-dependent. The relative ordering of E(\lambda, q) shifts with q. A knot may have \ell(K, q_1) \neq \ell(K, q_2) for q_1 \neq q_2. There are two regimes of q-dependence:

  1. Reordering: E(\lambda_i, q) and E(\lambda_j, q) swap relative position at some q^* \in Q. The filtration re-indexes but the set of operators at each level remains continuous.
  2. Vanishing: E(\lambda_\ell, q^*) = 0 at the LP boundary. The operator drops out of the filtration entirely, J^\ell collapses, and the level structure rebuilds. This is a categorical phase transition.

Magic configurations. A confined knot K at q is deeply confined at level \ell if and only if E_\ell(q) \ll E_{\ell+1}(q). In nuclear contexts, this corresponds to magic numbers A \in \{2, 8, 20, 28, 50, 82, 126\}. The nucleus sits at the bottom of an energy gap, far from the next LP-boundary. Its k_{\max}(K, q) jumps to a higher value than its non-magic neighbors.

Categorical interpretation. Conjecturally, the filtration J^\bullet(q) coincides with the \mathbb{Z}-grading filtration on the corresponding KLR module under the Brundan–Kleshchev isomorphism. This identifies the heuristic shadow-price ordering with a rigid homological grading.
